title: Hicham El Guerrouj: Mile Master
description: Middle-distance royalty—records, tactics, and Olympic pressure.

questions.question: Which Moroccan runner held the 1500m world record for over 20 years?
questions.explanation: Nobody has touched his mark since—Jakob Ingebrigtsen got within 0.73 seconds in 2024. He still owns the mile record too. Yet his Olympic story starts flat on the track.

questions.question: Hicham El Guerrouj crashed to the track in the 1996 Olympic 1500m final after clipping the heel of which rival, the eventual gold medalist?
questions.explanation: The Algerian stumbled but stayed up; El Guerrouj finished last, in tears. Minutes later King Hassan II phoned him: "For us, you are the winner." He kept a photo of the fall on his wall.

questions.question: Two years after that tumble, El Guerrouj took Morceli's 1500m world record in Rome—with what time?
questions.explanation: He sliced 1.37 seconds off Morceli's mark in a largely empty Stadio Olimpico, averaging under 55 seconds a lap. Nearly three decades on, it's still the world record.

questions.question: After his 3:26.00 world record, El Guerrouj finally won Olympic double gold in Athens in which two events?
questions.explanation: After the 1996 fall and a 2000 silver behind Noah Ngeny, Athens was redemption: he became the first man since Paavo Nurmi in 1924 to win both at one Games.

questions.question: In that Athens 1500m and 5000m double, which Kenyan did he edge by just 0.12 seconds in the 1500m final?
questions.explanation: 3:34.18 to 3:34.30, the closest Olympic 1500m final since 1976. The twist: Lagat later became a U.S. citizen and won the same 1500/5000 double at the 2007 World Championships.
